en: The Apadāna of the Elder Dhajadāyaka Ekapadumiya Chapter 3.3 *Therāpadāna*, Ekapadumiyavagga 3. Dhajadāyakattheraapadāna: I was once a merchant in the city of Benares, And I gave a banner to the Buddha Vipassī. By that root of merit, I have reached the world of gods; For eighty-four thousand aeons, I have been a king. Having passed away from there, I was reborn in heaven, And for eighty-four thousand aeons, I enjoyed celestial bliss. From that realm of gods, I passed away and was reborn here, In the human world, as a wheel-turning monarch. I ruled over the four continents, together with their islands, Possessing the seven treasures and the four great powers. Having performed such deeds, I have now attained this state; I have reached the final existence, and shall not be born again. This is the account of the Elder Dhajadāyaka, The thirty-third in the collection of the Elders’ Apadānas.
There was a teacher named Tissa,
the eldest in the world, a bull among men;
having seen the destruction of the three substrata, he—
The banner has been raised by me.
By that well-performed deed,
and by my volition and aspiration;
Having abandoned my human body,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three;
three hundred times indeed, I went there.
I exercised sovereignty over the gods;
and five hundred times,
I was a wheel-turning monarch.
I experience my own karma: a vast regional sovereignty, beyond counting and incalculable.
The well-performed deed for myself in the past:
that karma which I performed ninety-two aeons ago;
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of the gift of a banner.
If I so desired today, I could—
Including its forests and mountains;
I would cover it with linen cloth—
then the fruit of what I have done would be realized for me.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Dhajadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the third *apadāna* of the elder Dhajadāyaka.
